key_insight: A cell-centric, interpretable pathology model (C3PRO) matched top multiple-instance learning methods for PDAC diagnosis and prediction while making its decisions more understandable to pathologists.
clinical_relevance: This could improve trust and auditability of AI in pancreatic cancer pathology by linking predictions to recognizable cell phenotypes and stromal patterns with prognostic value.
method: Used a pathology foundation model to embed cell-centered tiles that include each cell and its surrounding neighborhood.
Clustered embeddings into recurrent morphological phenotypes and built a spatial graph to capture recurring tissue motifs.
Benchmarked C3PRO against four MIL frameworks for diagnosis, survival, and resectability prediction.
evidence_signal: Evaluated on 809 patients (825 diagnostic biopsies) with nested cross-validation, achieving AUC 0.958 for diagnosis, 0.617 for survival, and 0.696 for resectability.
watch_item: The phenotype vocabulary and prognostic signals need external validation and practical workflow testing before routine clinical use.
paper_title: An interpretable cell-centric representation of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma matches multiple-instance learning for clinical outcomes and leads to novel pathologist-driven histological biomarkers
